blocks.text: First run. Checking whether a roster already exists, and reading the goal before I design anything.

No workers besides the interviewer, so this organisation does not exist yet. Building two: one that drafts the newsletter on the clock, and one that reads what it wrote and writes down what happened — nothing else here writes memory on its own, so without that second one every future run of mine would find no evidence, forever.

input.name: newsletter-writer
input.description: drafts the weekly newsletter from what's worth telling this week
input.system_prompt: You are newsletter-writer. Each Monday you draft that week's newsletter for the shop's mailing list. Read kind=fact and kind=decision for anything worth mentioning; write the draft as a memory labelled kind=draft, name=<issue-slug>. Do not send anything — you only draft.
input.rationale: the charter's goal is a weekly newsletter; nothing existed to write one

input.name: newsletter-archivist
input.description: writes down what newsletter-writer produced, so there's evidence to steer by
input.system_prompt: You are newsletter-archivist. When newsletter-writer finishes, read what it produced and write ONE memory labelled kind=summary, name=<the issue slug>, plus a rolling summary labelled {kind: "rolling-summary", worker: "newsletter-writer"} so the next draft has context.
input.rationale: STEP 0 requires at least one worker subscribed to worker.finished, or no evidence is ever written

blocks.text: Wiring them up: the writer on a weekly clock, the archivist on the writer's completion, filtered so it doesn't wake itself.

input.rationale: the charter asks for one newsletter a week; Monday morning gives the shop the rest of the week to send it
filtered to newsletter-writer only, so newsletter-archivist never wakes itself

input.message: I built two workers. newsletter-writer wakes every Monday at 08:00 and drafts that week's newsletter from recent facts and decisions. newsletter-archivist wakes when newsletter-writer finishes and writes down what it produced, so there is evidence for me to steer by next run. Both are new — nothing existed before this. Every change here is in the changelog and can be reverted.
